rationale: Methods: outcomes were PDMS-2 and CUE; motivation appears only in interviews: "Semistructured interviews with parents and children, along with qualitative analysis, were conducted to evaluate their experiences with the exercise program"

Participants: "Participants were allocated to the gamified, traditional, or control group using a pseudo-randomized procedure constrained to produce approximately equal group sizes." Abstract calls it a "Quasi-experimental controlled trial." Also IMI was given to the two training groups only.
doubt: I2: does a pseudo-randomized allocation done and unconcealed by a single investigator count as random allocation?

rationale: Methods 2.3: no motivation scale; the only questionnaires are SUS ("was administered at 6 weeks, to the intervention group only"), BBS, Short FES-I, ACE-III and PASE. Motivation appears only in focus groups.
doubt: I2: two sheltered homes were randomised as clusters (one per arm); does a two-cluster allocation count as random allocation? Not needed for the decision.

rationale: Methods 2.5.4: instrument is the BREQ-2 ("Behavior Regulation in Exercise Questionnaire-2"). Both arms reported in Table 2: "EG 47.57 ± 6.75 49.87 ± 8.62 51.27 ± 5.56" and "CG 53.97 ± 17.22 55.97 ± 14.77 57.67 ± 14.09". Block-randomized, Kinect scored aerobic dance vs home aerobic dance video, 8 weeks, published 2025.
doubt: I1: is a Kinect aerobic dance programme whose score is joint-angle accuracy against a model a game with a goal or score pursued by movement? I3: the comparator is the same dance exercise by video with no score, a non-exergame arm. I6: Table 2 gives within-group P values and between-group P values per interval, with no clear single between-group test for BREQ-2 labelled as such.

rationale: Methods, Client Outcomes: no motivation instrument; the nearest measure is "Physical activities of the older adults were measured by the Chinese version of the Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly." Other measures: SF-12v2, GDS, GSES, SCS-R, eHealth Literacy Scale.
